title: X-SAT: An Efficient Circuit-Based SAT Solver
problem: Verifying equivalence of arithmetic circuits requires efficient SAT solving, but existing SAT solvers optimized for CNF struggle with circuit-specific structure and the high variable/clause counts in complex arithmetic circuits.
motivation: Circuit equivalence verification is fundamental to digital design, and arithmetic circuits are computationally expensive to verify with general-purpose SAT solvers.
method: X-SAT integrates Conflict-Driven Clause Learning (CDCL) with structural elimination techniques that reduce variables and clauses while preserving circuit topology. It enhances branching heuristics specifically for arithmetic circuit structure to guide search more efficiently.
key_novelty: Circuit-specific branching heuristics and structural elimination integrated into CDCL to exploit arithmetic circuit patterns that CNF-based approaches miss.
contributions: CDCL algorithm with structural elimination for circuit solvers
Circuit-aware branching heuristics optimized for arithmetic structure
Outperforms prior circuit solvers on all benchmarks
Matches or exceeds state-of-the-art CNF-based solvers on complex arithmetic instances

metrics.other: faster than CNF-based SAT solvers on arithmetic circuits

limitations: Paper does not discuss scalability limits or performance degradation scenarios.
primary_theme: efficient circuit verification via structure-aware SAT solving
